title: Scored request degradation: local stale-cache + tiered fallback reads for Redis/Kafka/DB
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: During cross-region incidents and downstream congestion (Redis timeouts, Kafka consumer lag, or DB saturation) our current failover strategies either (a) drop requests abruptly or (b) route everything to a single fallback which overloads that path. We need a graded, observable degradation mechanism that maintains SLOs for high-priority requests while exposing a predictable, explainable read-only degraded mode for lower-priority traffic.

Goal: Implement a scored-request degradation pipeline that: (1) assigns a resilience score per request (based on route, user-tier, SLA, and TTL of cached value), (2) attempts local stale-cache reads first, (3) falls back to replicated read-only replicas or cached materialized views, (4) triggers circuit-breakers and token-bucket shedders when downstream health crosses thresholds, and (5) emits rich metrics and traces to trace which degradation decisions were taken. This should support Redis (hot key cache), Kafka (consumer-side backpressure for event rehydration flows), and primary DB reads.

Constraints & non-goals: We will not change data correctness guarantees for writes in this ticket -- writes should continue to be strongly routed to primaries. This RFC focuses on read-path degradation only. Long-term cache warming and model-change strategies are separate tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Score computation available in request proxy and documented (route, user_tier, cache_ttl, biz_impact)
Local stale-cache read path implemented for Redis reads with configurable staleness window and opt-out flag
Tiered fallback read logic that tries read-replica -> materialized cache -> stale-cache in defined order with configurable timeouts
Circuit-breaker triggered when backend error rate or latency crosses thresholds and recorded as event in tracing
Token-bucket request shedder applied at network edge with per-tenant QoS budgets
End-to-end tests simulating regional dependency failure showing high-priority requests meeting 99th percentile latency SLO while low-priority requests are shed or served stale data
Dashboard panels added to Console: degrade-rate, stale-hit-rate, shed-rate, per-tenant QoS burn-down
Runbook updated with step-by-step mitigation and how to rollback degraded-mode behavior
work_done: Design spike (2d): measured existing stale-cache hit behavior and TTL distributions across routes (see confluence doc)
Prototype: added a proxy-level scored header and local stale-cache read hook (branch: feat/scored-degrade-proxy)
Simulated Kafka consumer backpressure: introduced short-circuit path for rehydrate jobs to read historical materialized store instead of live consumer when lag > 30s
Created unit tests for score calculation and deterministic fallback ordering
Drafted initial Console dashboard mockups for degradation observability (PR: github.com/redwood/prs/1234)
Security review: noted encryption-in-transit for cache replicas required (pending security signoff)
comments: 2026-02-12 - Ava Patel: Ran spike across three high-traffic routes. Observed that 27% of requests have cache TTL <= 60s and can be safely served stale for short windows without user-facing regressions. Attached analysis: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RD/scored-degrade-spike

2026-02-20 - Diego Martinez: Prototype deposited in repo; proxy exposes header `X-RW-Resilience-Score` and a new config `stale_read_window_ms`. Local stale reads return 95% fewer downstream connections in the trial environment.

2026-02-26 - Priya Shah (SRE): Suggested adding EWMA-based health measure for connection pools rather than raw error rate to avoid thrashing during short bursts. Agree to implement EWMA(10s, 60s) health signals.
2026-03-03 - Design review (Riley O'Connor): UX for Console should show per-tenant QoS budget and ability to raise/lower shedding thresholds in real-time. Created design ticket DES-412.

2026-03-09 - Diego Martinez: Integration test failing in k8s-e2e when circuit-breaker transitions rapidly. Suspect state race in pool resize logic; added short debounce and fixed test. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/1456
2026-03-12 - PM review (Maya Kline): Verified acceptance criteria mapping to customer impact stories; requested an explicit canary plan for Dedicated customers before wide rollout.
open_questions: What is the default customer QoS budget per month for hosted free-tier users? (affects default shed thresholds)
Should materialized caches be invalidated synchronously after a write in strong-consistency flows? (likely no; need to document eventual-consistency impact)
Do we expose a per-route opt-out so teams can disable stale reads for safety-critical features?

Run canary against 10% of traffic for two Dedicated customers and measure 99p latency and correctness delta (owner: Maya)
Add feature flag to toggle scored-degrade behavior per-tenant (owner: platform-api)
Ship runtime-1.24 canary with documentation and updated runbook
